title: Prove it like you mean it
kicker: World 6 · Prove It & Fix It · Level 3

job.text: Before you can mark the tool "done," add your own case that could actually break it — on a dimension you haven't tested yet — with its correct expected value, and show the whole set passing. So far you have tested a normal month, an empty month, and a refund month. A duplicate of one of those proves nothing new. In your own words you would ask the AI to add a case on an untested dimension; here you build that ask from the checklist.

rows: add one on an untested dimension
preview.more: seed-42 sales · year boundary (Dec→Jan) is still untested

naivePrompt: Add a test and we're done.
basePrompt: Add a test and we're done.

text.plain: State the correct expected total for the new case before you run it.
text.tech: Commit the expected value for the new case before executing it.

text.plain: Run every case, old and new, and show them all green.
text.tech: Execute the full case set including the new case and report all green.

moves.label: Call it done, it looks solid

text.plain: It's covered enough — call it done.
text.tech: Coverage looks fine — mark it done.

subChoices.label: A month spanning the year boundary (Dec→Jan) — an untested dimension
Another normal month like March — a duplicate

rules.claim: 4 of 4 green, including the year-boundary case with its committed value.
rules.feedback: You proved it like you mean it. You picked a case that could actually break it — a month spanning the year boundary — gave it the right expected total, and it held. That's a new dimension, not a repeat.
rules.lesson: Design a case that could fail, then show it doesn't.

output.source: a case set that reaches an untested dimension and holds

rules.claim: The new case can't fail differently from one you already have.
rules.feedback: That case can't fail differently from one you already have. Another ordinary month tests exactly what March already tested. A test that can only pass the same way isn't a new test. Try a dimension we haven't tried.
rules.lesson: A redundant case adds no proof.

output.source: a duplicate of a dimension already covered

rules.claim: Year-boundary case ran, but with no committed expected value.
rules.feedback: Good dimension, no answer attached. A year-boundary month is worth testing — but without a committed expected total you'll grade it to whatever it returns. State the correct number first.
rules.lesson: A good case needs the right answer attached.

output.source: a new dimension with no expected value

rules.feedback: "Add a test" without saying what kind just repeats what you have. Pick a case on a dimension you haven't tried, commit its expected value, and run the whole set. Otherwise you've added nothing.
rules.lesson: Proof means a case that could have failed, not another easy one.

hints.nudge: What input have we NOT tried that could trip it up?
hints.gap: Covered so far: normal, empty, refund. What about a month that spans a year boundary — December into January?
hints.moves: Choose the year-boundary (Dec→Jan) case, add Say its expected value and Show the whole set passing. Skip the duplicate month — it proves nothing new.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "add a test" → a duplicate that proves nothing.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: add a case on an untested dimension with its expected value, run the whole set → real proof.

template.plain: Add one case that could actually break this on a dimension we haven't tested yet, with its correct expected result, and show me the whole set passing.
template.tech: Add one case on an untested dimension, commit its expected value, and run the full set to show every case green.

notes: ChatGPT: ask it to name the untested dimensions first, then add a case for one.
Copilot in Excel: add a test row that's unlike the others — a boundary value, not a repeat.
A chat AI that can't run code: pick the weird input yourself and work out the answer before testing. Never accept "I added a test, all pass" without seeing it.
